concepts.title: Summary of the Story
concepts.definition: Sentila, a young Naga girl, dreams of becoming a pot maker like her mother Arenla and grandmother, but her mother wants her to become a weaver; whenever she can, Sentila secretly approaches expert potters to learn the clay craft and pursues her calling.
concepts.key_idea: A daughter's dream of the potter's wheel clashes with a mother's plan of weaving.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe102.txt story sections (Sentila, Arenla, learning the craft)
question_patterns: summarise the story in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Sentila wishes to follow her mother's and grandmother's pottery tradition.
Arenla prefers weaving for her daughter's future.
Sentila seeks out expert potters and practices quietly.

concepts.title: Character Sketches - Sentila and Arenla
concepts.definition: Sentila is passionate, patient and quietly determined, while Arenla is a loving but firm mother shaped by practical concerns; their differences are of dreams, not of love.
concepts.key_idea: Two strong wills, one bond: Sentila's passion meets Arenla's practicality.

solution_steps.explain: Determination, curiosity and love for the clay craft.
Hard work, practicality and deep motherly care.
Both mother and daughter act out of love and concern.

concepts.title: Theme - Tradition, Craft and Individual Choice
concepts.definition: The story celebrates traditional crafts like pottery and weaving while asking whether tradition should dictate an individual's calling; it honours heritage and personal choice together.
concepts.key_idea: Traditions live through learners, but each learner owns the choice of craft.
question_patterns: what is the theme of the story - explain

solution_steps.explain: Respect for craft heritage alongside personal choice.
Sentila's persistence and Arenla's mastery both honour craft.
Connect to vanishing crafts and young learners around you.
